widgets.name: WindowFrame
widgets.purpose: Root element of one window. Titled is the full app window (main and settings) with a TitleBar under it. Frameless is the borderless quick-add capture card, desktop only. Fills its window and holds the title bar, body and overlays.

values.when: h-screen w-screen, flex column, bg-surface-1, text-content-1, overflow hidden. Used by the main and settings windows. Window size (1180x760 default, 820x640 narrow, Settings 1180x760 at 0,0) is window configuration, not a variant.
rounded-panel, 1px border, w-screen, no TitleBar, light surface (dark grey in dark theme). Used only by the capture bar (desktop only).

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Frameless only. Handles Enter, Escape and Tab for the whole capture bar.

props.name: children
props.description: Titled: TitleBar and body row (PaneGroup) with overlays. Frameless: the capture bar rows.

widgets.role: none (document root; each desktop window is its own document)
widgets.keyboard: Frameless: root onKeyDown handles Enter, Escape and Tab for the whole bar. Titled: none.
widgets.platform: Desktop: each window is a real OS window; main and settings are native windows; capture is a separate frameless window. Web: no window chrome from the app; main is the app root page; Settings is a route, not a window; no capture bar.
widgets.open: Web presentation of Settings (route or dialog) is undecided. Capture bar is desktop-only and drops out of the web build. Merge: A's kind main and kind settings collapse into titled (B): both render the same frame (surface-1, full window); Settings identity sits in its content. A's name Window is dropped for WindowFrame. A's settings frame has no recorded fill, so surface-1 is assumed for it (confirm).

widgets.name: TitleBar
widgets.purpose: Header strip at the top of a window or of a pane. Window scope is the draggable window chrome on desktop and can hold WindowControls and the list tabs or project switcher. Pane scope is an in-pane header that does not drag.

values.when: h-13 (catalogue), items-stretch, border-b edge-2, bg surface-1. Measured 1180x46 (820x46 narrow). Drag region on desktop. Main and settings windows. The settings-about bottom hairline is this standard border (folded).
In-pane header (Trash). Not draggable. Border edge-1 per A (measured: 46px in the tree, 44px band in the shot). B folded this to edge-2; A kept, see open.
WindowControls at the leading edge (macOS style): main, settings and trash on desktop.
No window or pane controls. Web build, where the browser provides the chrome.

props.name: scope
props.description: Sets border token, height and drag region.

props.name: controls
props.description: Places controlsSlot at the leading edge.

props.name: controlsSlot
props.description: WindowControls, or a close TrafficLight for the trash pane.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Optional trailing slot (settings-general discard button). Not recorded as present in A, so a prop and not an axis.

props.name: children
props.description: ListTabs and Toolbar (window scope), project switcher, or the pane title content. Interactive children carry data-no-drag.

widgets.role: banner when scope is window and top-level; none when scope is pane
widgets.keyboard: The bar is not focusable. Window scope: the drag region is pointer only; double-click on a data-tauri-drag-region target calls getCurrentWindow().toggleMaximize() (TitleBar.tsx:43-46). Children keep their own keys.
widgets.platform: Desktop: drag region, double-click maximise and leading window controls on macOS; Windows caption placement is open. Web: no drag region and no window controls; the same bar is the app header with the project switcher and list tabs.
widgets.open: Height: catalogue h-13 is measured 46px. At 1rem = 14px, h-13 is 45.5px (rounds to 46), but h-11 (command input, 44px) and h-10 (capture title row, 40px) match 16px rem, so the rem base must be resolved before tokens are written (same conflict for CommandInput and InputGroup bar). Windows caption-control placement is open (no trailing rule in the catalogue). Pane border conflict: A edge-1, B edge-2; kept A's edge-1 because it is measured and visible; designer to confirm. Default controls: A none, B leading; kept none.

widgets.name: WindowControls
widgets.purpose: Cluster of three TrafficLight discs in a macOS-style group, with glyphs shown on group hover. Used in the window title bar, the settings windows and the trash pane close light.

values.when: Close, minimise and full screen all act. Main title bar, multi-inspector, filter panel, draft inspector.
Only close acts; minimise and full screen are inert. Settings windows and the trash pane close light (Close Trash).

props.name: focused
props.description: Window focus (useWindowFocused); lit when true, grey when false. Passed to each disc.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Closes the window, or the pane for Trash (setTrashOpen(false)). The caller sets the target.

props.name: onMinimize
props.description: Minimise action; inert when live is close.

props.name: onFullScreen
props.description: Full-screen action; inert when live is close. B's spelling onFullscreen is the same prop.

widgets.role: group, aria-label 'Window controls' (proposed)
widgets.keyboard: Not in the reference. Proposed: each live disc is a focusable button with its own label (Close, Minimize, Full Screen). Tab moves between live discs; Enter or Space activates; inert discs are skipped. No arrow navigation.
replaces: traffic-light cluster, settings (close live, others inert)
widgets.platform: Desktop only, macOS look. Web has no native window to close. Windows and Linux need their own caption controls; the catalogue has none.
widgets.open: Pane close: the Trash close light closes the pane, not the window. Same look; the caller sets onClose. B asks whether pane close should be WindowControls on desktop and an IconButton on web; decide one widget for both. Trash appears in both the all-live and the close-only rows in the catalogue (B); A records close-only. Settings cluster: source records disabled=[2] for the group, but the Light rows mark minimize and fullscreen inert (uncertain). Draft Light onClick handlers and settings-general and settings-shortcuts Light onClick targets were not read.

widgets.name: TrafficLight
widgets.purpose: One disc of a WindowControls group: close, minimise or full screen, live or inert.

values.when: Close disc. The only live disc in the settings windows. Red fill in the shot.
Minimise disc. Inert in the settings windows. Colour not recorded.
Full-screen disc. Inert in the settings windows. Colour not recorded.
Clickable; lit or grey with window focus.
Always grey, not focusable, no effect (built with minimizable(false) and maximizable(false) in settings-general).

widgets.role: button (proposed) with aria-label Close, Minimize or Full Screen; inert uses aria-disabled and is not focusable

widgets.platform: Desktop only. Web has no traffic lights (browser chrome). Windows caption buttons are an open choice and not this disc style.
widgets.open: The red close fill is a fixed traffic-light colour, not a token. The danger token is reserved for destructive actions, so close must not use it; no traffic-light token is recorded (uncertain). A's live/inert axis and B's disabled prop are one inert flag; B's focus axis is A's focused prop. The settings disabled=[2] conflict is recorded under WindowControls.

widgets.name: PaneGroup

Persistence of the split ratio is undecided. Unit mismatch: task panes size in percent of the group, the aside clamps in px (280 to 420). One rule is needed for both.

widgets.name: Pane

Right aside host, shrink-0, width from previewWidth clamped 280 to 420 (319 in recorded states). Hidden when previewOpen, trashOpen and filterOpen are all false (App.tsx:108). A merged the aside host and the side pane surface into one slot.

The fixed w-44 width (154px at 14px rem) needs a prop or a defaultSize mapping; unresolved. Settings-shortcuts sidebar fill is an estimate (not in elements.json), folded to surface; box approx [0,46,153,714]. Aside surface colour was not measured (A: side pane look bg-surface-1). Clamps: ratio 0.25 to 0.75 (App.tsx:78-82); previewWidth 280 to 420 px (App.tsx:110-115), which is 20rem to 30rem at 14px. Unit mismatch with percent sizes: see PaneGroup.

B's orientation and placement axes are folded into target and edge (same looks; A's target axis keeps the visible row and tab difference).

props.description: Overlay on web, separate window on desktop.

props.name: footer
props.description: A Footer row with the actions (Cancel and accept).

widgets.role: dialog (prompt) or alertdialog (confirm); aria-modal on web
widgets.keyboard: Escape closes (captureEscape). Tab and Shift+Tab are trapped inside (trapFocus). Initial focus on the first field is proposed. Enter activates accept only if set as the default (not in catalogue). Focus return to the opener is not recorded.
widgets.platform: Desktop: presentation window; each sheet is its own window with no Scrim; close by Escape or the close control; no outside-press dismissal for a window. Web: overlay with a Scrim; outside press dismisses; focus trapped.
widgets.open: The reference runs one destructive confirm in place (reset all settings button, ConfirmButton). The decision makes confirmations windows on desktop, so ConfirmButton may be replaced by Dialog kind confirm (undecided). B's kind sheet is named prompt here. Dropped duplicates: B's command palette panel is CommandPalette; A's sheet action row is Footer. The outside-press path and focus return are not confirmed (Overlay source not read). Palette and lightbox desktop presentation are undecided.

widgets.name: Scrim
widgets.purpose: Full-window layer behind a modal, a menu or the lightbox. Dims the window, and a press on it outside the panel dismisses. Also the invisible click-catcher under a context menu.
widgets.base: Radix Dialog Overlay (soft and strong-blur); a plain layer for none

values.when: bg-black/30 (oklab 0 0 0 / 0.3), no blur. Sheets and the command palette.
Strong dim plus backdrop blur, flex column, full window. Attachment lightbox. B's separate blur axis is folded here.
Invisible full-window hit area under a menu; catches clicks and right-clicks outside the menu.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Mousedown outside the panel dismisses the owning layer (B's onPress).

widgets.role: none; aria-hidden
widgets.keyboard: None; Escape belongs to the owning modal or menu.
widgets.platform: Web: under Dialog overlay, CommandPalette overlay and Lightbox overlay. Desktop: no scrim for dialogs or sheets (decision). The invisible click-catcher for menus is still needed on desktop unless native menus are used (undecided).
widgets.open: Lightbox: whether a bare click on the scrim closes it is not confirmed (Overlay source not read). The scrim colour is a literal (bg-black/30), not a token. Palette and lightbox presentation on desktop open.

widgets.name: Lightbox
widgets.purpose: Full-window viewer for one attachment: a stage that holds the preview and closes on empty space.

values.when: Web, or desktop if the lightbox stays in-window. Sits over Scrim strong-blur.
Desktop, if the lightbox is treated as a dialog window (undecided).

widgets.role: dialog (modal)
widgets.keyboard: Not recorded. Escape is not confirmed. The reference stage also holds prev and next chevrons, which are not in this catalogue.
widgets.platform: Desktop presentation is open. Web: overlay.
widgets.open: Treating the lightbox as a dialog for the desktop rule needs confirmation. Stage is px-16 pb-8 (a column Stack); the media wrapper stops the stage click from closing. Empty-stage click closes (onClose).

widgets.name: AttachmentPreview
widgets.purpose: Inline preview of one attachment inside the lightbox, chosen by its type. A failure switches to the EmptyState card.
widgets.base: none (native img, video, audio, embed and pre)

values.when: img with alt set to the attachment name, fitted to the stage, rounded-control, object-contain, shadow-2xl, draggable false. About 480x300 (16:10).
Native video with controls and autoPlay, rounded-control, shadow-2xl.
Panel in the Card look (surface-2, rounded-panel, px-8 py-10) with a 40px glyph (weight 200) and native audio controls with autoPlay.
Embedded viewer (type application/pdf), rounded-control, h-full w-full max-w-4xl.
Selectable pre in surface-2, 12.5px, leading-5, max-w-3xl, overflow-auto, p-5. Capped at 262144 characters.

props.name: autoPlay
props.description: Default true for video and audio.

widgets.role: image: img; video and audio: native controls; pdf: embedded viewer; text: pre
widgets.keyboard: Native media controls for video and audio (play, pause, seek). Text is selectable. PDF uses the browser or webview viewer's keys. Image has no action.
widgets.platform: PDF depends on a built-in PDF viewer in the browser or the desktop webview; desktop WebView support must be checked (open). Web media is served from the server; desktop media is read from disk.
widgets.open: Merged: B's MediaPreview is this widget (B's text kind omission is corrected from A). B's error fallback names Card; A's EmptyState card is kept. The PDF embed has no onError in either design, so a failed PDF never reaches the fallback. Zoom and pan are not evidenced. Image radius not measured.

widgets.name: AttachmentTile
widgets.purpose: Grid tile for one attachment: a thumbnail for images or a glyph for a remote link. Click opens it; drag carries it into a note.

values.when: Remote link: link glyph 22px, colour oklch(0.62 0.013 264). Click opens the link externally (api.openAttachment). Three-item context menu.
Local image: img alt empty, object-cover thumbnail when loaded. Click opens the lightbox at its index. Four-item context menu.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Click action: opens the lightbox or the link.

props.name: menuItems
props.description: Supplied by the caller: three for link, four for image.

props.name: draggable
props.description: Carries ATTACHMENT_MIME; a drop onto a note inserts a mention chip.

widgets.role: button; accessible name from name
widgets.keyboard: Enter or Space opens (native button). Right-click opens the menu; the context-menu key or Shift+F10 is proposed. Dragging onto a note has no keyboard path in the reference (open).
widgets.platform: Web: files are uploaded to the server, so thumbnails and the lightbox load from the server; the link opens in a new tab. Desktop: local files open from disk. How api.openAttachment opens a remote link on web is not read.
widgets.open: Tile is 94x94, radius 7px (B folds to rounded-control; radius to confirm), background oklch(1 0 0) is a literal, not a token. Menu item counts: link three, image four; the fourth image item is not named in either design. Keep one item set across platforms, dropping only items that need local disk (B).

widgets.name: MentionChip
widgets.purpose: Inline @mention chip for an attachment inside a note body. It is an atom: it cannot be typed into and deletes as one unit.

values.when: Click opens the attachment in the lightbox.
Click calls api.openAttachment.

widgets.role: none (inline atom); button if it becomes focusable (proposed)
widgets.keyboard: Click opens. Delete or Backspace removes it as one unit (the reference says it deletes as a single unit; the key is not recorded).
widgets.platform: Same.
widgets.open: Conflict: B lists this under notWidgets as owned by the rich-text editor family; A keeps it as a widget with its only recorded axis (source). Kept here with A's measured source until the family decision. Look is not measured. Present in note HTML only (count 0 in trees).

widgets.name: Toast
widgets.purpose: Brief notice pill at the bottom centre of the window, with an optional action. One toast at a time from the store. The wrapper passes clicks through everywhere except the pill.

values.when: Fixed bottom-5, full width, flex justify-center; viewport pointer-events none; the pill is pointer-events auto. Tree bounds 1180x41 at 0,702; pill 225x41 at 477,702.
Floating popover tone with lift shadow and radius control; animate-rise on entry. The only look in the catalogue (B's tone).

states: hidden (store toast is null; renders nothing)
widgets.role: status (polite live region)
widgets.keyboard: Action buttons are focusable once focus moves into the viewport. Radix Toast has a default hotkey (F8, moves focus to the viewport); set it explicitly. On web browser shortcuts take precedence; on desktop it must not act as a global hotkey. Escape to dismiss is recommended (B), not in the catalogue.
widgets.platform: Same position on both. Desktop: a toast raised from a separate sheet window must appear in that window, not the main one.
widgets.open: Dismiss rules (timeout, swipe) are not recorded. The store holds one toast; a second replaces the first (confirm). Pill radius is an estimate (about 6-8px); shadow and border are literals. The floating surface folds surface-2 and surface-3 into one popover tone (B), which also applies to the palette and menus; designer to confirm.

widgets.name: ContextMenu
widgets.purpose: Floating menu opened at the pointer for a task or a list tab. Picking an item closes it first.

values.when: At the pointer position (anchor x and y); the only recorded placement. Dimmed by Scrim none.

props.name: items
props.description: Rows and dividers (Separator inset menu between groups).

props.name: open
props.description: Shown while a menu is set (B).

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Outside mousedown, Escape, window blur or resize.

widgets.role: menu with menuitem rows (Radix; proposed)
widgets.keyboard: Escape closes. Outside mousedown closes. Window blur or resize closes. Right-click prevents the native menu and closes. Picking an item closes first, then calls onPick. Arrow keys move and Enter picks (Radix). Context-menu key or Shift+F10 is proposed.
widgets.platform: Desktop: window blur and resize close it; native OS menus are an option (undecided). Web: window blur means browser window or tab blur; preventing the browser's own menu on right-click is a choice to confirm; the native menu must remain in text inputs and the rich-text editor.
widgets.open: Width is content-driven: task menu 154x175, tab menu 158x145 (min-w-44, auto height; B folded the two). Panel radius not recorded. Triggers on task rows and list tabs are unverified; A keeps them in notWidgets, B lists them here (kept as notWidgets until a trigger is confirmed). Dropped duplicates: B's onSelect (onPick) and onOpenChange (onDismiss). B's pointer placement is A's anchored, since A records anchor x and y; conflict: B reads anchored as trigger-box positioning.

widgets.name: CommandPalette
widgets.purpose: Command palette: a 490px card near the top of the window with a search input and a list of commands.
widgets.base: shadcn Command (cmdk) inside a Dialog (CommandDialog, size palette)

values.when: Centred near the top, over Scrim soft. The recorded case.
Desktop option if the palette is treated as a dialog window (undecided).

widgets.role: dialog (modal) containing a combobox and a listbox (cmdk; proposed)
widgets.keyboard: Escape closes via onClose. Arrow keys move the active row (cmdk; proposed). The opening shortcut is not confirmed (useAppKeyboard not read). The active row is scrolled into view. Web browser shortcuts take precedence; on desktop a global hotkey pressed while the main window is focused is handled by the main window.
widgets.platform: Desktop: presentation open. Web: overlay; the opening shortcut must not clash with a browser shortcut.
widgets.open: Presentation on desktop is undecided. Width is min(35rem, 100%): 490px at 14px rem (560px at 16px); top edge at y 91; max-h 60vh. Opening shortcut not confirmed.

widgets.name: CommandInput
widgets.purpose: Input row at the top of the command palette: a leading glyph, the search input and a bottom rule.
widgets.base: shadcn CommandInput (cmdk), framed by InputGroup shape bar

values.when: Bolt glyph in the reference (at 355,102).

widgets.role: combobox on the input (proposed); the row is none
widgets.keyboard: Typing filters. Arrow keys move the active row in the list (cmdk; proposed).
widgets.platform: Same.
widgets.open: Row is h-11 with a 1px bottom border, measured 44px; h-11 at 14px rem is 38.5px, so this conflicts with the rem decision (see TitleBar).

widgets.name: CommandList
widgets.purpose: Scrolling list of command groups and rows. Keeps the active row in view.

values.when: Populated list of groups and rows.
Shows the empty message (palette-no-match).

props.name: activeId
props.description: Active row; scrolled into view (block nearest).

widgets.role: listbox with group headings (proposed)
widgets.keyboard: Active row scrolled into view. The keys that change the active row are on CommandPalette.
widgets.platform: Same.
widgets.open: Group heading style is not recorded. py-3, min-h-0, flex-1, overflow-y-auto. The palette results list is B's ScrollArea use; kept here.

widgets.name: TabList
widgets.purpose: Tab strip: the active project's list tabs in the title bar (horizontal), or the Settings section navigation (vertical). The New list button sits outside the tablist, because it is an action, not a tab.

values.when: Title-bar strip: flex h-full, items-stretch, min-w-0 flex-1, no-drag on desktop.
Settings sidebar list: flex column, gap-1.
Horizontal scroll when tabs overflow, scrollbar hidden (overflow-x-auto). Covers the list tab strip (A's ScrollArea horizontal hidden).
Tabs fit, no scroll. Used by the vertical settings list (its overflow is not recorded; fit assumed).

props.name: children
props.description: Tab items from the tabs family.

widgets.role: tablist; aria-orientation follows orientation
widgets.keyboard: Horizontal: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move between tabs. Vertical: ArrowUp and ArrowDown move to the next or previous section with wrap-around, selecting it and focusing its tab (SettingsWindow.tsx:186-196; onKeyDown at :265). Home and End are proposed.
widgets.platform: Same on web and desktop. On desktop the strip is no-drag inside the title bar. Tab drag-reorder is the tab family's job.
widgets.open: ListTabs keyboard handling for the horizontal strip is not in the catalogue (no onKeyDown read). Tab stop behaviour and Home and End keys are not recorded for Settings. Web Settings as a route is open.

widgets.name: TabPanel
widgets.purpose: Scrolling content of the active Settings section.

values.when: surface-2 token: the settings-general pane. Overflow-y auto, px-8 py-7.

widgets.role: tabpanel
widgets.keyboard: Scrolls with keys when focused. Proposed: tabIndex 0 on the scroll region when it overflows.
widgets.platform: Desktop Settings window. Web: open (Settings as a route).
widgets.open: Conflict: settings-general uses the surface-2 token; settings-shortcuts, settings-capture and settings-about record a literal oklch(0.995 0.001 255). Both designs keep one token; the literal is not a variant until someone confirms it is intended. B's ScrollArea raised tone for this pane is the same token.

widgets.name: ConfirmButton
widgets.purpose: Button that asks for a second press before it acts, inline, because the Settings window has no dialog layer.
widgets.base: none (a Button with a two-step state)

values.when: Ordinary action.
Destructive action (reset all settings); tone assumed from the decision.

props.name: label

states: confirming (after first click; from source only)
widgets.role: button

widgets.platform: Desktop Settings. Web and desktop should share Dialog kind confirm for destructive confirmations (open).
widgets.open: B lists the reset button under notWidgets as a shared Button with a danger tone and a two-step confirm. Kept here as ConfirmButton because the inline two-step is a behaviour users feel (A). Decision: confirmations are windows on desktop, so ConfirmButton may be replaced by Dialog kind confirm (undecided). Confirming state is from source only. The 28px height is from the catalogue.

widgets.name: InlineComposer

widgets.platform: Same.
widgets.open: Not in any recorded tree (count 0). Example: Subtask title, Enter to add. B's Row editing prop is this widget's job and is dropped from Row. The parent row is not in these files.

No rule (settings-about header look not recorded).

The dot is Indicator and its accent colour conflicts with the accent rule (see DropIndicator). B has no SectionHeader; its section accent dot is in Indicator.

widgets.name: Indicator

values.when: 6px rounded-full (h-1.5 w-1.5). Section accent dot and filter activity dot (StatusDot).
2px by 16px (h-4 w-0.5). Draft accent caret in the title row; task inspector accent tick at the header edge (size not measured, folded here).

widgets.keyboard: None.
widgets.platform: Same.

Accent is reserved for primary action and selection: the active filter dot and the caret and tick are conflicts or uncertain; a status token may be needed, or neutral for the filter dot. Accent-as-selection for the caret and tick is uncertain. Tick size is not measured; caret width is 2 to 3px (estimate).

widgets.name: Spinner
widgets.purpose: Busy indicator beside a status text, shown while a screen capture runs.

widgets.role: status (proposed), with the label

notWidgets.reason: Routed placeholder in PreviewPanel, chosen when selectionTasks.length is above 1. No look of its own; content is Stack (inspector body root) inside a Pane aside, built from Row, Footer, Card and Pane (B). Same in both designs.
Routed placeholder in PreviewPanel for one selected task. No look of its own; content is Stack and a Pane aside. Same in both designs.
Routed placeholder in PreviewPanel when draftListId is set and no task is selected. No look of its own; content is Stack and a Pane aside. Same in both designs.

Routed placeholder that replaces PreviewPanel in the aside when trashOpen is set. No look of its own; content is built from Pane aside, TitleBar scope pane, Toolbar strip, ScrollArea, Row and Separator (A; B cites Footer and Row).

notWidgets.variant: filter and sort panel slot (not in tree)
notWidgets.reason: Routed placeholder for filterOpen when trash is not open. No look of its own; content uses RefineRow, Indicator, Separator and a Pane aside.
Routed overlay placeholder with onClose, shown only when paletteOpen. Its visible panel is CommandPalette (Dialog size palette over Scrim soft); the slot has no look.
Always-mounted, non-visual provider for in-app sheets; renders no box while idle. It mounts Dialog instances (the Dialog portal does this job).
Non-visual provider that supplies context-menu state to the window; the ContextMenu root does this per window and has no visual node.

Invisible spacer whose only job is to be a window drag region (data-tauri-drag-region). Desktop only. Covered by the TitleBar window-scope drag region; a Stack with dragRegion and no look to build (listed under Stack.replaces in B).
Positioning wrapper with no look of its own around one 21x21 Search options icon button, which belongs to the button family. Stack can render it (B lists it under Stack.replaces).

Disabled placeholder for the task completion check on a draft. It is the same control as the task-row round check and should be rendered disabled, not as a second copy. Whether the task-row family defines the round check is uncertain (B).
Unverified trigger: no code, tree or capture confirms it (count 0); TaskRow2 has no onContextMenu. Nothing to build until verified. B lists it under ContextMenu.replaces; kept here until verified.
Unverified trigger: the ListTabs labels have no context handler (count 0). Nothing to build until verified. B lists it under ContextMenu.replaces; kept here until verified.
